prompt: On the unit circle, the angle $0^\circ$ lands on the point $(1, 0)$. Cosine is the SHADOW ACROSS. What is $\cos 0^\circ$?
hint: Cosine is the FIRST number in the point $(x, y)$ — how far across you are.

hints.text: Cosine is the FIRST number in the point $(x, y)$ — how far across you are.
The point at $0^\circ$ is $(1, 0)$, so the across number is $1$.

explanation: The unit circle is a circle of radius $1$ centred at the origin.
Every angle names one point on it, and that point is always $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ — cosine is the shadow ACROSS, sine is the height UP.
At $0^\circ$ you sit at the far right edge, the point $(1, 0)$, so $\cos 0^\circ = 1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the clock hand
steps: Point a hand of length 1 straight to the right, like a clock hand aimed at 3 o'clock. That is the 0° direction.
Its tip is 1 unit across and 0 units up. The across number IS the cosine, so cos 0° = 1.

alternativeExplanations.title: The radius is the ruler
steps: The circle has radius 1, so the tip of the hand is never more than 1 unit from the centre.
At 0° the hand lies flat along the across-direction, spending ALL of its length going across. Across = 1, up = 0.
